analysis_claims.universe: Endpoint-specific valid baseline/follow-up pairs among returners, retaining original assignment. Eligible bases are all enrolled in each arm. Missing counts describe each wave across that enrolled arm and can overlap; they must not be summed to obtain pair exclusions.
analysis_claims.weighting: Supplied fixed weight_base; both waves use the same endpoint-specific paired weights. Values transcribed and rounded from supplied analysis tables.

analysis_claims.universe: Separate valid-case distributions at each wave, pooled across assignment. Baseline eligibility is all enrolled; follow-up eligibility is returned questionnaires. These are not paired changes or a conversion funnel.
analysis_claims.weighting: Supplied fixed weight_base; each distribution uses its own valid-case denominator. Values transcribed and rounded from supplied tables.

findings.proposition: Assignment produced a larger observed-pair awareness increase: assigned households rose from 30.83% to 58.76% (+27.93 percentage points), versus 31.37% to 45.70% (+14.33 points) in control. The assignment contrast was +13.59 points, supporting an awareness objective for a further controlled campaign test.
findings.claim_strength: Positive assignment-on-change evidence among observed pairs; significant within the declared primary family.
findings.qualification: SE 2.08 points; pointwise 95% CI 9.52 to 17.66; raw p=6.032e-11, Holm p=1.810e-10. Control/assigned paired bases (N, weighted N, ESS): (1016,999.79,876.62)/(960,965.21,834.41); eligible bases (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30). This is not a recovered full-cohort effect. Control growth cannot be attributed to one specific mechanism.

findings.proposition: Consideration growth did not distinguish assignment from control: top-two consideration rose 28.68% to 37.04% under assignment (+8.36 points) and 31.49% to 39.86% in control (+8.36 points). The incremental estimate was -0.01 points.
findings.claim_strength: No detected assignment difference; not evidence of equivalence.
findings.qualification: SE 1.75 points; pointwise 95% CI -3.44 to 3.42; raw and Holm p=0.9962. Control/assigned paired bases (N, weighted N, ESS): (1015,1000.17,877.62)/(966,973.61,839.32); eligible bases (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30). Full five-category paired and separate wave distributions are retained in analysis_claims. Consideration was asked of everyone after the same description, not only aware respondents.

findings.proposition: Reported use also provides no demonstrated incremental benefit: assigned households rose from 6.19% to 8.80% (+2.61 points), versus 5.51% to 9.10% in control (+3.59 points), giving a -0.98-point assignment contrast. The evidence supports testing how awareness translates into use before claiming a business return.
findings.claim_strength: No detected usage benefit; follow-up testing is a researcher recommendation.
findings.qualification: SE 0.877 points; pointwise 95% CI -2.70 to 0.74; raw p=0.2641, Holm p=0.5281. Control/assigned paired bases (N, weighted N, ESS): (1007,993.81,868.83)/(969,973.30,842.04); eligible bases (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30). The negative estimate does not establish harm or zero effect. Use is self-reported, not transactions; costs and revenue are absent, so ROI cannot be estimated. A follow-up test should prespecify a meaningful downstream effect and improve outcome recovery.

findings.proposition: Selective follow-up limits generalisation. Control returned 1070 questionnaires and assignment 1019, with weighted return rates of 75.98% and 72.38%. Returners already had higher baseline consideration and lower budget pressure than nonreturners.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence of selection; direction of outcome bias is unestablished.
findings.qualification: Return-rate eligible=valid bases (N, weighted N, ESS), control/assigned: (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30); no numeric missingness. Nonreturners/returners have eligible bases (711,723.48,622.07)/(2089,2076.52,1808.85). Their baseline consideration top-two rates were 21.99%/30.13%, valid bases (691,704.14,604.75)/(2028,2018.38,1756.82), missing 97/98/99=(9,3,8)/(36,13,12). High/very-high budget pressure was 49.20%/33.68%, valid bases (692,703.06,605.98)/(2036,2026.36,1762.90), missing=(12,2,5)/(34,11,8); baseline structural exclusions=0. The supplied profile audit also shows returners had higher awareness, use and digital confidence and fewer children. Arm profiles differ both before and after attrition; apparent balance on individual measures cannot repair selection. Endpoint pair counts and separate numeric/structural exclusions are retained in analysis_claims.

findings.proposition: Logged receipt and recall comparisons would overstate what random assignment established. Recipients' follow-up consideration advantage was 19.12 points, almost identical to their 19.15-point baseline advantage. Recallers' follow-up advantage was 37.24 points, but they already led by 32.35 points at baseline.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive associations with substantial pre-existing differences; not causal exposure effects.
findings.qualification: Receipt=0/1 eligible=valid consideration-pair bases (N, weighted N, ESS): (944,1003.75,820.43)/(1037,970.04,903.73), total 1981, no grouping exclusions. Recall=0/1 eligible=valid subgroup bases: (1040,1107.13,906.03)/(844,760.65,741.87), total 1884; 97 of the 1981 consideration pairs lack valid recall and are excluded. Baseline and follow-up comparisons use the same people within each grouping. Recall was measured after outcomes; neither receipt nor recall was randomised. These gaps do not identify mediation or an effect among compliers.

findings.proposition: The invitation policy achieved incomplete receipt and control crossover: logged receipt was 70.16% under assignment and 24.54% in control. This is a comparison of invitation policies in a setting with organic exposure, not a comparison of universal exposure against no exposure.
findings.qualification: Receipt-rate eligible=valid bases (N, weighted N, ESS), assigned/control: (1400,1412.94,1220.30)/(1400,1387.06,1210.61), with no missingness or structural exclusions. Among returned valid-recall respondents, 34.18% of logged recipients reported no recall, while 15.73% without logged receipt reported recall. These conditional eligible=valid bases are respectively (1048,981.02,912.94) and (939,985.15,816.54); they exclude nonreturners and invalid recall before grouping. Logs do not prove attention, and recall is not a verified exposure measure.

findings.proposition: Households with children have a stronger stated need, but no established campaign-response advantage. Very/extremely stressful meal planning was reported by 56.48% with children versus 36.56% without. None of the three prespecified children interactions passed Holm adjustment.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive audience need; inconclusive prespecified heterogeneity.
findings.qualification: Stress eligible bases (N, weighted N, ESS), children/no children: (1090,979.51,985.73)/(1710,1820.49,1471.74); valid bases (1060,950.38,958.69)/(1686,1791.67,1451.12); missing 97/98/99=(16,6,8)/(17,4,3), structural exclusions=0. Children-minus-no-children assignment interactions in points: awareness -5.07 (95% CI -13.46 to 3.32; raw p=.2358, Holm .4717), consideration +4.27 (-2.95 to 11.48; raw .2464, Holm .4717), usage +2.81 (-0.98 to 6.59; raw .1459, Holm .4378). In cell order no-children control, no-children assigned, children control, children assigned, eligible bases are (874,922.52,748.57), (836,897.97,723.19), (526,464.53,477.07), (564,514.97,509.01). Awareness valid bases: (666,692.78,568.95), (591,631.00,510.05), (350,307.01,317.68), (369,334.21,332.54); consideration: (663,690.86,567.85), (598,641.29,516.17), (352,309.32,319.63), (368,332.32,331.99); usage: (662,693.43,566.03), (600,642.15,518.45), (345,300.38,314.09), (369,331.15,332.65). Need can motivate a children-focused test; these results do not justify preferential targeting on effectiveness grounds.

findings.proposition: Recalled message ratings were favourable, but cannot explain the awareness result or identify a proven optimisation lever. Agreement was 76.74% for clarity, 70.52% for relevance and 75.90% for believability; relevance's numerical position is a hypothesis for testing.
findings.claim_strength: Selected-recaller descriptive diagnostics; no superiority or causal-driver inference.
findings.qualification: All three items have eligible base (N, weighted N, ESS)=(891,800.64,781.76), with 1909 structural exclusions. Clarity/relevance/believability valid bases: (862,773.02,755.96)/(854,770.28,747.66)/(852,765.17,749.26); numeric missing 97/98/99: (22,3,4)/(25,6,6)/(33,3,3). Full distributions from strongly disagree through strongly agree: clarity [0.47,3.62,19.17,30.88,45.86]%; relevance [2.06,8.58,18.84,27.02,43.49]%; believability [1.39,6.73,15.97,29.27,46.63]%. Weighted Pearson correlations are clarity–relevance .506, clarity–believability .504 and relevance–believability .544; pairwise valid bases respectively (828,745.18,724.59), (823,737.54,723.46), (816,735.48,716.01), from the same eligible recaller base. These shared impressions were not tested for ranking and do not establish latent or causal drivers.

beats.headline_intent: Lead with awareness evidence and the unestablished downstream benefit.
beats.analytical_relationship: Compare assigned and control changes separately for each endpoint; distinguish evidence of awareness improvement from nonsignificant consideration and usage contrasts.

beats.headline_intent: Bound the conclusion to the households with observed outcome pairs.
beats.analytical_relationship: Qualify the assignment findings using attrition, item completeness and baseline selection.

beats.headline_intent: Explain why receipt and recall do not provide an alternative campaign-effect estimate.
beats.analytical_relationship: Contrast random assignment with observational exposure groupings, preserving their separate universes and baseline differences.

beats.headline_intent: Separate the priority audience's need from evidence of superior response.
beats.analytical_relationship: Use prespecified interaction tests to assess heterogeneity; use meal-planning stress only as descriptive audience context.

beats.headline_intent: Recommend a controlled follow-up test of downstream response with better outcome recovery.
beats.analytical_relationship: Use awareness as the supported result, usage as the unresolved business outcome, and audience need and message ratings as test hypotheses rather than established explanations.

method_notes: Only the supplied study content was inspected. No tools, external sources, raw-data files or delegated agents were used. analysis_claims transcribe supplied table evidence rather than introduce raw-data estimates; evidence_refs use exact JSON Pointer table paths.
The service, respondents and target profile are fictional. The eligible online-recontact panel is not a national probability sample, and no result describes real UK prevalence.

Primary estimates retain random assignment and use each endpoint's own valid observed pairs. Consideration codes 4–5 are top-two; valid codes 1–3 are zero for that binary endpoint. Codes 97/98/99 and structural blanks are excluded, never imputed as No or zero.

weight_base transports the baseline age-by-online-grocery profile and remains fixed. Weighted N is a sum of weights, not population size. Kish ESS measures weight concentration and does not replace paired-change variance.

Inference uses the supplied independent-household fixed-weight normal approximation: arm variance is n/(n-1) times sum[w²(D−weighted mean D)²]/(sum w)². Contrast variance adds arm variances; interaction variance adds four disjoint cell variances. All reported intervals are pointwise 95%, not simultaneous.

Holm adjustment controls each declared three-test family separately at .05. It does not provide joint .05 control across both families or exploratory analyses. No reported primary or interaction estimate has degenerate zero variance.

Percentages and bases are rounded for readability. Full precision, paired missingness details and five-category distributions remain available at the cited table paths. Wave-specific missing counts may overlap and must not be added to infer unique pair losses.

The exploratory older digital online-grocery subgroup has only 22 control and 21 assigned awareness pairs: insufficient base. Its percentages, lift, intervals and p-values are suppressed, and it supports no targeting recommendation.

Numerical ordering alone does not establish superiority. Nonsignificance does not establish zero effect or equivalence. Attrition uncertainty is omitted by the fixed-weight intervals; no receipt effect, mediation, full-population effect, sales impact or ROI is established.
